headline: South Asia: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN.
- Persian Gulf Region: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations.
- Asia: Musk ordered to preserve records on Ukraine’s Starlink access by Democratic US senators.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Air Force adopts new Force Design focusing on sensors and autonomy.
- Military Times, 22 hours ago: US Air Force adopts new Force Design focusing on sensors and autonomy.
The Air Force's new Force Design 2026 outlines a shift toward artificial intelligence, autonomy and integrated sensors to counter emerging threats.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 2027 Rhodes Scholar hopes to transform healthcare through tech.
- Jamaica Gleaner, one day ago: 2027 Rhodes Scholar hopes to transform healthcare through tech.
For Somesh Sharma, being named Jamaica’s 2027 Rhodes Scholar is more than a dream fulfilled. It is a chance to turn opportunity into lasting impact and give back to the country that shaped him. “I am feeling very happy, elated. [I] can’t believe it. I’m very thankful to receive this award. it’s been an incredible journey,” the 22-year-old said after the announcement was made on Thursday at King’s House in St Andrew.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Buenos Aires Herald, one day ago: Milo J, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso win big at 2026 Latin Grammys.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian drone strike kills man on scooter in Zaporizhzhia Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian drone strike kills man on scooter in Zaporizhzhia Oblast.
A 45-year-old civilian riding along the central road of Kushuhum has been killed in a Russian drone attack.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: One killed and 10 injured, including child, in Russian strike on Pavlohrad.
A Russian attack on the city of Pavlohrad has killed one person and injured ten others, including a 7-year-old boy.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Estonia outlines details of Ukrainian attack on Russian missile ship in Baltic Sea.
Colonel Aron Kalmus, Deputy Commander of the Estonian Division, which brings together Estonian forces and allied units assigned to it, has described how several Ukrainian drones struck the Naro-Fominsk, a Russian Baltic Fleet corvette, during a large-scale attack on the port of Ust-Luga.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Police officer shields injured boy, 9, during repeat Russian attack in Sumy Oblast.
Police officers in Sumy Oblast have rescued a 54-year-old woman and her nine-year-old grandson after a Russian attack caused a fire at their home. When Russian forces attempted a second drone strike, one of the officers shielded the boy with his body.
Southern Europe - bottom line: EU, UK ‘Concerned’ as Kosovo Moves Against Hague Court’s Powers Again.
- Balkan Insight, one day ago: EU, UK ‘Concerned’ as Kosovo Moves Against Hague Court’s Powers Again.
The EU and the UK warn Kosovo MPs not to pass an amended law curbing the powers of the Hague-based Kosovo Specialist Chambers war crimes court without consultations with international allies.
- Balkan Insight, 2 days ago: Bosnian Court Convicts Three of Wartime Abuses of Civilian Prisoners.
The state court handed down 41 years of prison time to three defendants for committing war crimes against detained civilians in Bosanski Novi in 1992.

A nuclear treaty and the US's war on Iran are among priority topics for China, Russia and US leaders.

A grenade exploded at a business in the northern Arab town on Saturday, killing a woman and wounding three others as police opened an investigation.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Russian casualties ‘reach 450,000’: What that means for the Ukraine war.
Leaked Russian records reveal a war toll that falls hardest on older men, poorer regions and foreign recruits.

- Africanews, 8 hours ago: DR Congo: At least 44 dead in attack by Islamic State-linked gunmen.

The warrants target exiled journalists, activists, an ex-minister, and former military officers who face several terrorism-related charges.
- Africanews, 2 hours ago: Microsoft apologises for global outage and rules out cyberattack.
The tech giant said on Saturday that service has now been restored across Teams, Outlook, and its other products, ending the shutdown.
South Africa - bottom line: Namibia: NSC Defends Awards Representation Amid Nomination Concerns.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: Namibia: NSC Defends Awards Representation Amid Nomination Concerns.
[New Era] The Namibia Sports Commission (NSC) has defended the representation and integrity of the 2026 Namibia Annual Sport Awards (NASA), acknowledging that only 25 of its 68 affiliated federations submitted nominations while maintaining that the awards are gaining momentum.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan on Friday called for an immediate end to military provocations in the Gulf and renewed regional diplomacy as the United States, Iran and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries exchanged sharply conflicting accusations at a UN Security Council meeting on attacks against shipping and threats to maritime security. The debate highlighted growing concerns that the confrontation could disrupt international trade, energy supplies and food shipments while increasing the risk of a wider regional conflict.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Pakistan, 16 other countries, condemn Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital.
Pakistan and 16 other countries,on Saturday condemned the Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, calling on Tel Aviv to protect civilians and medical facilities and ensure the sustained and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid to the Palestinian enclave. The deadliest single strike since Israel’s elections last month hit the surgery ward of Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis early on Thursday, killing at least six Palestinians, including a 13-year-old boy, and wounding nearly 30 others.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Major among 4 troops martyred, 24 terrorists killed during operations in KP and Balochistan: ISPR.
Four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, the military’s media wing said on Saturday. In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that since Nov 13, armed forces have been conducting multiple IBOs “around Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki, including area domination and patrolling of the Quetta-Taftan National Highway (N-40) to keep it secure for local traffic and sustain operations”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: ‘A moral red line’? World on cusp of autonomous weapons revolution.
Lethal autonomous weapons powered by artificial intelligence are set to revolutionise warfare, but there is no proper regulatory or legal framework governing the new technology. A conference starting Monday at the United Nations in Geneva will discuss how to establish curbs and prohibitions on such weapons, called killer robots by some. But some analysts doubt the discussions at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) will keep pace with the fast-changing weapons. AFP looks at three key questions ahead of the conference.

- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 11 hours ago: Musk ordered to preserve records on Ukraine’s Starlink access by Democratic US senators.
Democratic US senators have told Elon Musk to preserve all records related to his company SpaceX’s restrictions on Ukraine’s use of its Starlink and Starshield satellite services. Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of ‌Starlink, is vital for frontline communications and drone operations in their defence against Russian drone and missile attacks. But in mid-October, Ukrainian officials complained that the service had been restricted without explanation or warning,...

- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Cleaner, smarter, big data: the PLA’s bet on ‘sunshine’ military recruitment.
The Chinese military is mining big data to get better recruits and stamp out corruption in the march towards its centenary next year. As part of an overhaul called “end-to-end sunshine” recruitment, the People’s Liberation Army has been commanded to use data-driven systems across the the enlistment process to build a military “focused on war readiness”. The orders came this month from the general offices of the Central Military Commission and State Council and mark a renewed push to eradicate...
- South China Morning Post - China, 7 hours ago: How Chinese custom ‘chong xi,’ or ‘clashing with joy,’ can counteract misfortune.
In ancient China, when a man became seriously ill, his family might arrange a wedding for him in an attempt to drive away the disease. The custom is called chong xi, literally translated as “clashing with joy”. Its rationale is that a happy event could lift one’s spirits and thereby dispel illness or other misfortunes. In practice, if a man who was already engaged became seriously ill, his family might move his wedding forward. If he did not yet have a fiancée, his family might hastily find him...

- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Trump considers holding back on Iran strikes even as military keeps options open.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Dragged, beaten with sticks, fists: J'khand woman killed over Rs 500 owed by dead man.
Six individuals were arrested in connection with the murder of Jinggi Bankira in Hadimara village. The dispute arose over a debt of Rs 500 owed by Reena Gope's deceased husband. Following an altercation, Bankira was attacked by the accused, leading to her death from severe injuries. Evidence collected during the investigation included blood-stained items linked to the crime.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Shooter Who Killed Mad Sandhu Arrested, Wanted To Attack Bollywood Actor.
The arrested men have been identified as Vikas Thakur (alias Vicky), a resident of Punjab's Jalandhar, and Deep (alias Deepak Singh). Deepak was wanted in the shooting and murder of Punjab-based influencer Mad Sandhu in Amritsar on October 3.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Iran Dials Up Cyber Attack Pressure, Targets Supermarkets, Water Systems.
Iran began building its cyber capabilities in the early 2000s, with Israel emerging as its primary target. Over time, its operations expanded to include Gulf rivals such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Microsoft ‘deeply sorry’ for global outage that could have billion-dollar impact on Australia.
- The Guardian - Australia, 10 hours ago: Microsoft ‘deeply sorry’ for global outage that could have billion-dollar impact on Australia.
Experts say disruption exposes ‘Australia’s reliance on foreign technology’ as software giant says services being restored Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The Microsoft outage could be a disaster for the Australian economy that forces some small businesses to close, with costs expected to run into the billions of dollars, experts have warned. The US software company has said it is “deeply sorry” for a widespread outage that caused disruption to millions of users, organisations and businesses across the globe – and that it has “addressed the underlying issue”.

Sources connected to the Australian bowling group say they all spoke to investigators as part of the inquiry into Cape Town ball tampering, which runs counter to claims by David Warner.
- ABC News Australia, 14 hours ago: 'Plastic farmers' in Indonesia unaware of the dangers of burning waste.
For decades, locals in East Java in Indonesia have been burning plastic waste but may not have been aware of the health consequences.
